pictures.scene: Metsu, The Sick Child — a woman in a brown jacket and a blue skirt sits holding a listless child across her lap, the child lying back against her in a yellow coat and a little white cap with its legs hanging down limp and its eyes turned out of the picture, the woman's head bent right over it and her hand closed gently round its arm, a red cloth thrown over the chair at her side, the plain whitewashed wall behind them with a rolled map hanging on it and a dark framed painting of the crucifixion up in the corner, when jesus had concluded his discourse in the hearing of the people, he went to capernaum, there a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: Veronese, Christ and the Centurion — the grey-bearded captain goes down on one knee in the street in polished steel armour and a crimson cloak, his face turned up and his hand laid flat on his breastplate as he speaks, a young soldier in a plumed helmet kneeling in behind him with both arms round him to hold him up and a long halberd standing up into the sky above them, Christ standing over him barefoot in a rose robe and a deep blue mantle with His head bent down toward him, the bald and white-bearded elders crowded in close at His shoulder and watching, the pale domed building and the open evening sky behind, when the centurion heard about jesus, he sent some jewish elders to ask him to come and heal his servant, they came to jesus and pleaded with him earnestly, this man is worthy to have you grant this
pictures.name: pd_veronese_centurion

pictures.scene: Brandon, A Scene in the Synagogue — a bearded man in a pale gold prayer shawl carries the dressed scroll of the law high against his shoulder at the top of the steps with its silver crowns and bells showing above him, his face lifted and his mouth open in the chant, men in wide black hats and shawls pressing in behind him on the platform, another in a heavy gold-edged shawl standing down on the right with his hands together, a boy in a long white tunic holding up two lit tapers at the foot of the steps, the congregation in their seats behind the carved rail at the left with two small children looking over it, the broad patterned carpet laid down the stairs and the dark pillars and arches of the hall going up over all of them, for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue, so jesus went with them, but when he was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message, lord, do not trouble yourself, for i am not worthy to have you come under my roof
pictures.name: pd_brandon_scene_in_a_synagogue

pictures.scene: Gericault, An Officer of the Imperial Horse Guards Charging — a mounted officer wheels his grey horse round on the ridge in the middle of the smoke, turning in the saddle to look back over his shoulder with the curved sabre held out low in his right hand and the other hand up on the rein, a tall black fur cap with a red plume on his head and a gold-laced dark green jacket with a fur-lined pelisse hanging from his shoulder, white breeches and a red sash, the spotted leopard skin thrown over the saddle and the horse rearing up with its mane blown forward and its eye rolling, the dark broken ground under its hooves and the battle smoke and a far gun carriage away at the right, that is why i did not consider myself worthy to come to you, but just say the word, and my servant will be healed, for i myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me, i tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes, i tell my servant to do something, and he does it
pictures.name: pd_gericault_an_officer_of_the_imperial_horse_guards_charging

pictures.scene: Uhde, Grace Before the Meal — Christ stands barefoot in the middle of a poor cottage kitchen in a long worn blue robe with a faint ring of light behind His head, His hand lifted small and open in front of Him as He speaks the blessing, the labourer of the house standing close in beside Him in a patched blue jacket and wooden clogs with his head bowed and his own hand put out toward the table, a boy waiting by the chairs behind them and the mother in white standing at the far side of the round table, the white cloth laid with empty soup plates and spoons and a loaf, the plain lime-washed wall and the open door letting the daylight in across the scrubbed board floor, when jesus heard this, he marveled at the centurion, turning to the crowd following him, he said, i tell you, not even in israel have i found such great faith, and when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health
pictures.name: pd_uhde_the_mealtime_prayer

pictures.scene: Courbet, A Burial at Ornans — a funeral procession stands crowded together on the bare ground outside the town, a server in a white surplice holding up the tall black processional crucifix so that it rises against the grey sky over all their heads, the old priest in a black cope with a heavy white-fringed stole reading the office with his head bent down, two boys in white albs and red caps beside him, one looking up at the cross and the younger carrying the brass holy water pot down at his knees, the pallbearers in wide black hats and white hoods pressing in on the left and the beadles in scarlet robes and red caps at the right, the bare hills and the little town on its rock standing away behind them, soon afterward, jesus went to a town called nain, his disciples went with him, accompanied by a large crowd, as he approached the town gate, he saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow, and a large crowd from the town was with her
pictures.name: pd_courbet_a_burial_at_ornans

pictures.scene: Kotarbinski, The Raising of the Widow's Son at Nain — Christ stands in the middle of the road outside the town in a long white robe with His right arm flung up high over the bier and His other hand hanging open at His side, His face lifted and His long hair falling back, the dead young man laid out at the left under a heavy black pall edged with gold with sprigs of white blossom scattered over him and the bare wooden handles of the litter running out across the bottom of the picture, the mother crouched down beside it in a dark blue mantle and a black head cloth with her hands twisted together and her eyes turned up to Him, the mourners pressed in behind in striped shawls and turbans watching without a sound, the flat-roofed white houses and the round tower of the town standing up on the hill behind under a heavy grey sky, when the lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said, do not weep, then he went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still, young man, he said, i tell you, get up
pictures.name: pd_kotarbinski_widow_of_nain

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, An Old Woman as the Prophetess Anna — a very old woman sits alone out of the dark in a wide fur-lined hood with a gold-embroidered band across the brow and a soft grey veil drawn in under it round her face, every line and fold of the worn old face lit up and her eyes turned down and away in thought, a stiff pleated white ruff standing up at her throat and a heavy black gown fastened with a wrought silver clasp, a dark fur-edged mantle with long tasselled cords hanging down from both shoulders, her two swollen hands folded together low in her lap over a red cloth, the bare brown wall going back into shadow behind her, and the dead man sat up and began to speak, then jesus gave him back to his mother, a sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified god, a great prophet has appeared among us, they said, god has visited his people
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_prophetess_anna

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, A Street in Jerusalem — the morning sun comes down the narrow stone street and strikes the great pointed archway that spans it, the honey-coloured ashlar of the gate house above lit right up with its latticed oriel windows and a pigeon or two sitting along the string course, overhanging timber balconies and shuttered screens leaning out from the tall houses on the right over a dark shop arch, the whole crowded lane running away under the arch into the haze of the next street with awnings strung across it, an old man in a white head cloth and a dark robe walking out of the shadow into the light with his staff, a boy in a red coat coming down beside him with a dog at his heel, traders squatting over their baskets and a seller leaning out of his stall along the sunlit wall, the worn paving stones shining all down the foreground, and the news about jesus spread throughout judea and all the surrounding region, then john's disciples informed him about all these things
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Burnand, The Disciples Running — two men run side by side out of the dawn light with their heads thrust forward and their eyes fixed on something ahead of them out of the picture, the younger one on the left with his dark hair blown back from his face and his mouth open for breath, his hands caught together in front of his chest and his long pale robe streaming back from him as he goes, the grey-bearded older man pressing on at his shoulder in a rust-red cloak with a dark mantle flying from it, his brows drawn up and his hands clutched in against him, the sky behind them one wide wash of yellow morning with a few violet clouds drawn across it, so john called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the lord, are you the one who was to come, or should we look for someone else, when the men came to jesus, they said, john the baptist sent us to ask, are you the one who was to come, or should we look for someone else
pictures.name: pd_burnand_disciples_running_colour

pictures.scene: Ancher, Sunshine in the Blind Woman's Room — an old blind woman stands alone at the end of the scrubbed kitchen table in a black head cloth and a long black skirt with a worn blue-green bodice, her sightless eyes open and turned a little aside and her face lifted toward the warmth she can feel, one hand laid flat on the table edge to keep her place and the other closed loosely at her side, the low sun coming in through the small paned window and throwing two bright squares of light up onto the bare wall behind her, a glass jar and a few odds and ends standing in the sun on the sill and the table end, the open red-brown shutter at the right and a dark spindle-backed chair pushed in at the table in front of her, the plain board floor going off into shadow below, at that very hour jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and he gave sight to many who were blind, so he replied, go back and report to john what you have seen and heard, the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor
pictures.name: pd_ancher_solskin_i_den_blindes_stue

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a great crowd of country people packed together in a clearing in the wood to hear the preacher, the gaunt man in a coarse brown tunic standing up in a gap in the middle of them with both hands put out as he speaks and pointing away to one side, an old man in a long red robe and a dark-bearded man in blue standing close in behind him, the hillside of listeners banked up all round in black hoods and white linen head cloths and broad straw hats, boys who have climbed the trees for a view sitting astride the branches overhead, the near ones seen only from behind, a broad straw hat and a woman's yellow mantle filling the bottom of the picture and a baby looking back over a shoulder, the heavy trunks and the dark leaves closing the clearing in on every side with one gap of pale sky at the right, blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of me, after john's messengers had left, jesus began to speak to the crowds about john, what did you go out into the wilderness to see, a reed swaying in the wind
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Van Dyck, The Children of Charles the First — three royal children stand side by side in a palace room in front of a heavy dark green curtain looped back on a gold cord, the eldest girl at the left in a stiff white satin gown with deep lace at the shoulders and cuffs and a string of pearls round her throat, her fair curls dressed with a red ribbon and her hands resting quietly in front of her, a smaller sister beside her in a white lace cap and a long white gown with scarlet sleeves showing through, the young prince at the right in a suit of rose-red silk with a broad falling lace collar and a jewel at his breast, red hose and rosettes on his shoes, his hand laid on the head of a great hound that stands as high as he does, a thick patterned Turkey carpet spread under their feet and the pale wall and sky showing in the corner behind, otherwise, what did you go out to see, a man dressed in fine clothes, look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces, what then did you go out to see, a prophet, yes, i tell you, and more than a prophet
pictures.name: pd_van_dyck_the_five_eldest_children_of_charles_i

pictures.scene: Bol, The Angel Appearing to Elijah — an angel in a long pale robe with a gold-worked collar and dark tasselled cords hanging from the shoulders stands over the sleeping prophet in the dark of the wilderness, his fair curling hair falling to his shoulders and the great wings spread up into the shadow behind him, one hand put out low over the old man to wake him and a dark flask carried down in the other, the prophet lying stretched out on the ground at the right in a red robe and a brown cloak with a cloth wound round his head, his eyes still shut and his cheek pressed into his wrist, his other hand fallen open and empty on the bank beside him, the embroidered edge of his cloak spread out across the bottom of the picture and the black trees closing in overhead, this is the one about whom it is written, behold, i will send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you, i tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than john, yet even the least in the kingdom of god is greater than he
pictures.name: pd_bol_the_angel_appearing_to_elijah

pictures.scene: Reymerswaele, The Tax Collectors — two clerks lean over the counting table in a dim office, the one in front in a blue gown and a huge red shaggy hat that hangs down over his shoulders, a pair of round spectacles pushed askew on his nose as he bends low and writes out the account in a great open ledger with a quill, a gold ring on his finger and his sleeve dragging across the page, the second man crowding in at his shoulder in a green hood and a red doublet, his lined face screwed up and his eyes turned straight out of the picture, one finger jabbed down at the figures and his other hand picking the coins off the table where they lie scattered in their little heaps, a shelf behind them stacked with sealed papers and rolled documents and a brass candlestick, the carved panelling going up into shadow above, all the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged god's justice, for they had received the baptism of john, but the pharisees and experts in the law rejected god's purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by john
pictures.name: pd_reymerswaele_the_tax_collectors

pictures.scene: Bruegel, Children's Games — the whole open square of a town given over to children at play, scores of them scattered across the bare sandy ground in blue and red and brown smocks, one lot rolling and tumbling in a heap down the red railing at the left, boys riding each other pick-a-back and others hauling at one another in a tug of war in the middle, a girl bowling a hoop along the bottom edge and a boy trundling a barrel beside her, children turning somersaults over a long trestle in front of the town hall and balancing head down on its rails, little ones squatting over knucklebones and spinning tops in the corner, girls carrying a basket of fruit between them and others at a ring game under the arcade, a boy up a wall on stilts, faces leaning out of the windows above, the tall pale town buildings closing the square in and a strip of blue sky and a church tower showing away at the top left, to what, then, can i compare the men of this generation, what are they like, they are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, we played the flute for you, and you did not dance, we sang a dirge, and you did not weep
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_kinderen

pictures.scene: Kramskoi, Christ in the Wilderness — Christ sits alone on a low block of stone in the middle of a waste of broken rock, barefoot and worn thin after the long fast, a heavy dark blue-grey mantle pulled right round Him over a faded red robe, His elbows set on His knees and His two hands locked hard together in front of Him, His head bent forward and His eyes fixed on nothing at all, the stony ground running away flat and grey in every direction with loose splinters of rock scattered over it, the first pale light of morning along the horizon behind Him with one low band of pink cloud lying across it, for john the baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, he has a demon, the son of man came eating and drinking, and you say, look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners
pictures.name: pd_kramskoi_christ_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Perov, The Refectory — a rich lady comes into the vaulted hall of the monastery in a wide lilac silk gown and a white lace shawl with a bonnet on her head and a folded parasol hanging from her wrist, her chin up and her eyes looking straight ahead of her, the black-robed monks bowing and spreading their hands to welcome her in and an old gentleman in a dark tailcoat with a star on his breast and white trousers walking at her elbow, a monk flung right down on his face on the stone floor in front of her skirt, a crippled beggar woman on the ground at the right lifting both arms to the party with a ragged child clinging beside her and another child stretched out barefoot on the flags, the brothers at their reading desks going on with the office in the shadow at the left, the painted vault and the arched window and the gilt frames of the hall rising over the whole room, but wisdom is vindicated by all her children, then one of the pharisees invited jesus to eat with him, and he entered the pharisee's house and reclined at the table
pictures.name: pd_perov_kloostermaaltijd

pictures.scene: Bouts, Christ in the House of Simon — Christ sits at the end of the long white-clothed table in a plain grey-blue robe with His hand raised in front of Him in blessing and His eyes turned quietly down to the floor, the host beside Him in a jewelled blue cap and a green gown leaning in with his hand flat on the cloth and his mouth open to object, round loaves and a green glass and a whole fish on a pewter dish laid out across the table, the woman stooped right down on the tiled floor at His bare feet in a green bodice and a blue skirt with a red mantle spread out behind her, her loose fair hair gathered in her hand and drawn over His foot to dry it and her other hand pressed flat on the tiles to hold herself up, the little white alabaster jar and its lid standing open on the floor beside her, the bench and the bare grey wall behind and a column and a green river valley showing through the opening at the left, when a sinful woman from that town learned that jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume, as she stood behind him at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair, then she kissed his feet and anointed them with the perfume
pictures.name: pd_bouts_anointing

pictures.scene: Dou, Old Woman Reading — an old woman sits turned away into the shadow with a heavy book held up open in both hands, her head bent low over it and her eyes running along the printed column, every crease of the old face and the loose skin of her working hands lit by the light that falls on the pages, a pale linen band wound round her brow under a soft fur cap, a thick dark blue mantle with a broad fur collar fastened at her throat with a gold clasp, the two wide pages covered in black letter with a little woodcut set into the text, the plain dark green wall going back into nothing behind her, when the pharisee who had invited jesus saw this, he said to himself, if this man were a prophet, he would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching him, for she is a sinner, but jesus answered him, simon, i have something to tell you, tell me, teacher, he said
pictures.name: pd_dou_overdenking

pictures.scene: Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a money changer sits at his counting table in a wide black fur hat and a brown gown, his eyes down and his face intent as he lifts a coin to the little hand balance and holds the beam steady between his fingers, loose coins and gold rings and a few pearls lying scattered across the table in front of him, his wife beside him in a bright red gown with a grey fur-edged collar and a white linen headdress, a page of her illuminated prayer book turned half over under her hand while her eyes slide away from it to the scales, a small round convex mirror standing on the table between them with a window and a seated figure caught in it, a shelf behind them carrying a pewter dish and an apple and a stack of worn books, two men were debtors to a certain moneylender, one owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty, when they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them, which one, then, will love him more
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Garofalo, Christ Washing the Disciples' Feet — Christ kneels down on the stone floor in a deep red robe with a white linen cloth tied round His waist, a fine gold halo of rays about His head, both hands in the shallow brass basin washing the foot of the old disciple who sits before Him, the water running off the heel in bright threads back into the dish, the white-bearded disciple drawn back on his seat in a blue tunic and a great fold of yellow mantle over his knees, one hand pressed flat on his own chest and his face turned down at what is being done to him, the other disciples standing close behind in green and red and dark cloaks with their heads together, one pointing and another leaning in to see, the pale panelled wall and a stone pier rising plain above them all, i suppose the one who was forgiven more, simon replied, you have judged correctly, jesus said, and turning toward the woman, he said to simon, do you see this woman, when i entered your house, you did not give me water for my feet, but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair
pictures.name: pd_garofalo_christ_washing_the_disciples_feet

pictures.scene: Velazquez, The Waterseller of Seville — an old water carrier in a worn tawny cloak stands out of the dark beside his great earthenware jars, his lined face turned down in profile and his grizzled chin and hollow cheek caught by the light, one scarred hand closed round the handle of the big pale jug that fills the bottom of the picture, the other holding out a tall clear glass of water brimming with it, a boy in a white collar and a dark jacket taking the stem of the glass in both his hands and looking up with his eyes fixed on the old man, a dim third face drinking from a cup in the shadow between them, a second broad-bellied jar standing on the bench at the left with the wet gleam running down its shoulder, the bare dark wall shutting the whole thing in behind, you did not greet me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing my feet since i arrived, you did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_waterseller

pictures.scene: Guido Reni, The Penitent Saint Peter — an old apostle is turned half away into the dark with his face lifted and his mouth fallen open in grief, the light running over his bald brow and every deep line of the forehead and the long white curling beard, his eyes brimming and looking up and away at nothing in the shadow, one great gnarled hand clasped hard over the other against his chest with the knuckles standing out, a blue mantle slipped down off the shoulder and a fold of gold-ochre cloak gathered up under his arm, the thin working neck and the worn shoulder bare, the plain olive-brown ground going from light at the right into black at the left with the faint ring of a halo drawn across it, therefore i tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much, but he who has been forgiven little loves little, then jesus said to her, your sins are forgiven
pictures.name: pd_guido_reni_the_penitent_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Friedrich, Morning in the Riesengebirge — the sun is coming up over range after range of mountains seen from a high summit, the far ridges fading from violet to pale blue one behind another until they are lost in the light along the horizon, white mist lying in the valleys below and filling the hollow at the left, the broken red rock of the peak rising steeply at the right with the morning sun warming its edges and the dark heather clinging in the clefts, a slender wooden crucifix standing up on the very top of the rock against the empty sky, a woman in a long white dress climbing the last step with her hand stretched up and a man taking hold of it to draw himself up after her, the wide dawn sky above them washed from cream at the skyline into soft blue, but those at the table began to say to themselves, who is this who even forgives sins, and jesus told the woman, your faith has saved you, go in peace
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_morning_in_the_riesengebirge

lines.text: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, This man is worthy to have You grant this,
for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.
So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.
When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.
And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.
Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, Do not weep.
Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. Young man, He said, I tell you, get up!
And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. A great prophet has appeared among us! they said. God has visited His people!
And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
Then John's disciples informed him about all these things.
So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?
When the men came to Jesus, they said, John the Baptist sent us to ask, Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?
At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.

So He replied, Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.
After John's messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.
I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God's justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God's purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, He has a demon!
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!
But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.
Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee's house and reclined at the table.
When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.
When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him, for she is a sinner!
But Jesus answered him, Simon, I have something to tell you. Tell me, Teacher, he said.
Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?
I suppose the one who was forgiven more, Simon replied. You have judged correctly, Jesus said.

And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.
Then Jesus said to her, Your sins are forgiven.
But those at the table began to say to themselves, Who is this who even forgives sins?
And Jesus told the woman, Your faith has saved you; go in peace.
